name: Push API + Notifications
free_limits: MDN: 'Baseline — Widely available ... available across browsers since March 2023'. Compatibility data (PushManager): Chrome 42, Edge 17, Firefox 44, Firefox Android 48, Safari 16 ('Notifications are supported on macOS Ventura and later'), Safari on iOS 16.4 with the note 'Notifications are supported in web apps saved to the home screen'; iOS in-app webviews: not supported. WebKit: 'A web app that has been added to the Home Screen can request permission to receive push notifications ... in response to direct user interaction.' So on iPhone it works ONLY for an installed Home Screen web app, never in a Safari tab.
hosting_required: none (browser API); needs a service worker and VAPID keys on the server side
verification_note: Opened the MDN Push API page, MDN's browser-compat-data file for PushManager and the WebKit announcement https://webkit.org/blog/13878/web-push-for-web-apps-on-ios-and-ipados/. MDN's rendered compatibility table does not load through the fetch tool, so per-browser versions are read from MDN's own compat-data JSON.

name: Badging API (navigator.setAppBadge)
free_limits: MDN: 'Limited availability — This feature is not Baseline because it does not work in some of the most widely-used browsers.' Secure context only. Compatibility data for setAppBadge: Chrome/Edge desktop 81 ('Windows and macOS since Chrome 81', 'ChromeOS since Chrome 91', 'Linux offers no universal badging API'); Chrome Android: NOT supported; Firefox: NOT supported; Safari 17 ('installed web apps on macOS Sonoma and higher'); Safari on iOS 16.4 ('Badging is supported for web apps saved to the home screen'). Safari note: 'Passing 0 as an argument will clear the badge instead of displaying an unnumbered dot.'
verification_note: Opened the MDN Badging API page, the MDN setAppBadge page and MDN's compat-data Navigator.json (second half, where setAppBadge sits). Works on iPhone only for an installed Home Screen web app; does not work on Android Chrome at all. Feature-detect and treat as a nicety.

name: Screen Wake Lock API
free_limits: MDN: 'Baseline 2025 — Newly available. Since March 2025, this feature works across the latest devices and browser versions. This feature might not work in older devices or browsers.' Secure context only. Compatibility data: Chrome 84, Firefox 126, Safari 16.4; Safari on iOS full support from 18.4 - between 16.4 and 18.4 it was partial: 'Does not work in standalone Home Screen Web Apps' (WebKit bug 254545).
verification_note: Opened the MDN page and MDN's compat-data WakeLock.json. An iPhone older than iOS 18.4 running the app from the Home Screen will not hold the screen awake.

verification_note: Opened the MDN API page, the MDN SyncManager page and MDN's compat-data SyncManager.json. Chromium-only: no iPhone, no Firefox. An offline queue needs its own fallback (retry on app open / on the 'online' event). 'WICG' as the standards venue is from memory.

verification_note: Opened the MDN manifest reference page and MDN's compat-data share_target.json. An installed web app cannot appear in the iPhone share sheet; Android Chrome only.

name: Barcode Detection API (BarcodeDetector)

name: StorageManager (navigator.storage.persist / estimate)
free_limits: MDN: 'Baseline — Widely available ... available across browsers since December 2021.' Secure context only. verification_note: Opened the MDN page and MDN's compat-data StorageManager.json. estimate() is missing on iOS 15.2-16.x; feature-detect it. 'WHATWG Storage Standard' as the home spec is from memory.

name: Network Information API (navigator.connection)

verification_note: Opened the MDN page and MDN's compat-data NetworkInformation.json. Chromium-only hint; absent on every iPhone and in Firefox, so it can only ever be an optional enhancement.

name: CSP violation reporting (Reporting API, report-to, report-uri)
free_limits: Reporting API on MDN: 'Baseline 2026 — Newly available. Since March 2026, this feature works across the latest devices and browser versions', 'Some parts of this feature may have varying levels of support.' The `Report-To` HEADER is 'No longer part of the Reporting API but still supported by some browsers' - use `Reporting-Endpoints`. CSP `report-uri` is marked Deprecated, and 'in browsers that support report-to, the report-uri directive is ignored'; MDN: 'until report-to is broadly supported you can specify both'. Compatibility data: CSP report-to - Chrome 70, Safari 16.4, Firefox 149 (very recent); report-uri - Chrome 25, Firefox 23, Safari 7.
hosting_required: none (browser API / HTTP headers); needs an endpoint in the app to receive the reports
verification_note: Opened the MDN Reporting API page, the MDN report-uri page (https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Reference/Headers/Content-Security-Policy/report-uri) and MDN's compat-data for the Content-Security-Policy header. Send both directives: Firefox only gained report-to in 149 and older browsers still need report-uri. The two report body formats differ (application/reports+json vs application/csp-report) - from memory, not read today.
